purpose: Recover pooled world-boss/end-stage constructors, callback state machines, and the DS:88AE stage gate used by faithful entity behavior recreation.

pool.interpretation: World bosses are pooled callbacks. They do not appear as ordinary ARE dispatch entries; constructors allocate a record, install a callback, link child/helper records, and publish an END sprite slot.

stage_gate.interpretation: The byte is an authored boss/end-sequence stage gate. It is independent of the pending-effect budget DS:880C; 01F7:4519 accepts either gate, but the two values do not advance together.

states.2: kill helper child, choose slot 900/0x3B6, write stage 3
states.3: emit effects; after 16 cycles write stage 4

static_recovery.cross_world_variants: World-specific constructors use different slots, velocities, child links, damage thresholds, and state counts; the shared pattern is a pooled callback with movement/attack, damage-triggered transition, effect emission, exit, and child replacement.

runtime_w1l4_probe.fixture: Native main-tree W1L4 selected through the in-game level selector

observed.interpretation: The authored W1L4 fixture enters the END child callback set with DS:88AE=1. The bounded run did not reach a later stage-writer breakpoint, so it proves the active END callback topology and gate value, not the full timed transition sequence.

runtime_controlled_damage_probe.fixture: Native W1L4 END pool; debugger replaces the live A234 child callback with the original W1 B25D damage callback, seeds matching DS:87DE rows, then promotes that same record to B33B after the native stage-2 write.

observed.row_matching: B25D consumed five coordinate rows at the live object position; the row x word was cleared and object+0x2C advanced from 0 through 5.
observed.stage2_helper_action: B33B cleared the +0x36 helper callback, toggled the END slot from 0x385 to 0x384, and reached B61A.
observed.stage3_timing: The reduced trace waited natively through the +0x38 timer and captured B791 after the +0x44 burst counter exceeded 0x0F; it did not breakpoint every identical frame callback.
observed.stage5_return: The post-write B84C return observed DS:88AE=5, callback 01F7:487F, and sprite slot 0xFFFF on the promoted record; the final pool active count was 4.

runtime_controlled_damage_probe.interpretation: This is controlled callback-path evidence, not an authored damage/completion run: the fixture deliberately rewrites one live A234 callback and seeds the shared row table. It proves that the recovered native W1 damage/main callbacks implement the five-hit gate and stage progression 1->2->3->4->5, including helper kill, effect-loop timing, exit, and post-stage child replacement. It does not identify the retail producer that delivers damage rows or the completion handoff into DS:85DB/DS:85D4.

remaining: Capture the authored damage/completion producer that feeds DS:87DE rows or invokes the world-boss damage callbacks; the native callback state machine is now controlled-verified.
Capture the authored completion producer and downstream reload/resource handoff after the controlled DS:85DB -> 01D7:4F10-4FAF selector advance; 01D7:5017/5038/5047 remains unobserved dynamically.
Correlate DS:880C pending-effect increments with Wind/UFO row producers and the player 01F7:38EC trigger.
Resolve WOLKE-specific rendering/descriptor selection after the 01D7:4EA0 consumer.
confidence: Static world-specific state machines and the controlled W1 callback progression are high-confidence raw-segment/runtime recoveries. Native W1L4 confirms the pooled END topology and DS:88AE=1; the authored damage/completion producer and cross-world runtime timing remain open.
